response: It's good that you're watching for this — combination products make accidental acetaminophen overdose a real risk in home care. Per the label, harm is associated with exceeding the maximum recommended daily amount across all acetaminophen-containing products, so the first thing is to total up every source. Early warning signs in the first 24 hours are nonspecific — nausea, vomiting, sweating, low energy — and importantly, serious liver injury may not be obvious until 48–72 hours, so don't wait for dramatic symptoms before calling her clinician or Poison Control. I'd rather not frame a specific 'point of no return,' but if you're ever worried she's taken too much, contact Poison Control or her hospice team right away.
